agent_profiles.note: Installing a plugin copies its agents/*.toml into the plugin cache and stops there. Codex reads custom agent profiles from $CODEX_HOME/agents, which no packaging path creates, so the profiles sit inert until the synchroniser runs.

context_injection.conclusion: A skill with no agents/openai.yaml is injected into the model context. The absence of the explicit-only canary is evidence rather than a null result because two other canaries appear in the same recorded request.
context_injection.documented_at: plugin-creator skill reference shipped inside the codex 0.147.0 binary

admin-scope-resolution.reason: `admin` is in the 0.147 SkillScope enum but has no local origin on a developer machine: it needs a managed enterprise policy source, which is not configured here

agent-profile-packaging.how: checked for $CODEX_HOME/agents after installing all eleven plugins

context-injection-policy.how: three repo-scope canaries in one turn, read from the outbound request body

explicit-resolution-per-plugin.how: every skill directory in source compared against skills/list by qualified name

isolated-source-discovery.how: all eleven tracked plugins installed into a disposable home and listed back

removal-stops-resolution.how: one plugin removed and the listing re-read in the same home

search-scope-resolution.how: user, repo and system scopes each returned rows in one listing

skill-execution.reason: executing a skill requires a model to choose it; this round is offline. Every row below states that a skill was OFFERED, never that it ran.

findings.statement: Twenty-five skills across eight plugins carry no agents/openai.yaml, so they take the documented default and are injected into every model context. Only saga and verified-workflows declare explicit-only, and tests/test_explicit_skill_invocation.py asserts exactly those two plugins and is silent on the rest.
Skill scopes in 0.147 are user, repo, system and admin. Planning language that calls them Global, Workspace and Personal does not match the runtime enum.

limitations: Offered is not executed. Nothing here shows a model choosing or running a skill.

Skill discovery is not confined to CODEX_HOME. Even with a disposable home the listing included the operator's own ~/.agents/skills at user scope, so the user count is repository skills plus whatever that directory holds.
The admin scope was not exercised; no managed policy source exists on this machine.

method.kind: isolated plugin install plus offline turn capture
method.listing_instrument: codex app-server, JSON-RPC skills/list over stdio
method.note: Every plugin was installed from this worktree into a disposable CODEX_HOME through `codex plugin marketplace add` and `codex plugin add`, so discovery is measured against repository source rather than against whatever the operator already had installed. The injection rows come from a real turn assembled against a local Responses API stand-in, so the outbound request is read without any model call.
